:::{#exr-generalization-error}
#### Score a fitted model on a car it has not seen

A prediction rule $\fitted(\cdot)$ has been fitted to a training set $\mathcal{T}$
of $n$ observations $(x_1, y_1), \ldots, (x_n, y_n)$,
such as the 20 training cars of @exr-overfitting.
A new car $(X_0, Y_0)$ is then drawn from the same population,
independently of $\mathcal{T}$.

1. Holding $\mathcal{T}$ fixed,
   write the average squared [prediction error](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-error)
   that $\fitted$ would make over all such new cars,
   as an expectation.
2. Which parts of your expression do you know,
   and which do you not know?
3. The training RMSE of @exr-overfitting
   is the square root of the
   [mean squared error of the predictions](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-mse)
   $\fitted(x_1), \ldots, \fitted(x_n)$.
   What does that mean squared error use in place of your expectation?

:::
